title: OLE Analysis Workflow
text: vignette demonstrates open-label extension (OLE) phase analysis workflow using difference--differences () synthetic control method (SCM) estimators proposed Zhou et al. (2024) estimating long-term treatment effects control group switches treatment.

title: OLE Analysis Workflow

title: Simulation Workflow for OLE Phase
text: vignette demonstrates Monte Carlo simulation evaluating difference--differences () estimators proposed Zhou et al. (2024) open-label extension (OLE) phase.

what: 1. Simulate a dataset for OLE study
title: Simulation Workflow for OLE Phase
code: # Initialize an empty data list set.seed(2023)  data_matrix_list <- list() ntrial <- 500  # Specify the significance level alpha alpha <- 0.05  # Specify the true effect size at the end of the OLE study true_effect_long <- 0  # Specify column names covariates_col_name <- c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "x5") outcome_col_name <- c("y1", "y2", "y3", "y4") treatment_col_name <- "A" trial_status_col_name <- "S" # Sequentially adding in datasets for (trial_iter in 1:ntrial) {   # simulate 300 sample   normal <- copula::normalCopula(param = c(0.8), dim = 4, dispstr = "ar1")    # ========== generate internal covariates =============   X_int <- simulate_X_copula(     n = 200,     p = 4,     cp = normal, # copula     margins = c("binom", "binom", "binom", "exp"), # specify marginal distributions     paramMargins = list(       list(size = 1, prob = 0.7), # specify parameters for marginals       list(size = 1, prob = 0.9),       list(size = 1, prob = 0.3),       list(rate = 1 / 10)     )   )    X_int$x4 <- round(X_int$x4) + 1   X_int$x5 <- 30 + 10 * X_int$x1 + (7) * X_int$x2 + (-6) * X_int$x3 + (-0.5) * X_int$x4 + rnorm(200, mean = 0, sd = 10)    varnames <- c("1", paste0("x", 1:5))    # ============ generate external covariates ==============   X_ext <- simulate_X_copula(     n = 100,     p = 4,     cp = normal, # copula     margins = c("binom", "binom", "binom", "exp"), # specify marginal distributions     paramMargins = list(       list(size = 1, prob = 0.7), # specify parameters for marginals       list(size = 1, prob = 0.9),       list(size = 1, prob = 0.3),       list(rate = 1 / 10)     )   )    X_ext$x4 <- round(X_ext$x4) + 1   X_ext$x5 <- 50 + 10 * X_ext$x1 + (2) * X_ext$x2 + (-1) * X_ext$x3 + (-0.3) * X_ext$x4 + rnorm(100, mean = 0, sd = 10)    varnames <- c("1", paste0("x", 1:5))    # ============ Specify outcome models ==============   model_form_x_t1 <- setNames(c(10.0, 0.05, -1.5, -1.0, -0.2, -0.1), varnames) # 1.5*A, sigma = 4.0   model_form_x_t2 <- setNames(c(6.0, 0.5, -0.5, -1.0, -0.3, -0.06), varnames) # 1.8*A, sigma = 4.0   model_form_x_t3 <- setNames(c(5.0, 1.9, 1.4, -1.3, -0.4, -0.15), varnames) # 1.6*A, sigma = 4.0   model_form_x_t4 <- setNames(c(1.2, 1.0, 2.0, -0.5, -0.4, -0.10), varnames) # 2.5*A, sigma = 5.0    outcome_model_specs <- list(     list(       effect = 0, model_form_x = model_form_x_t1, # from data: true_effect = 1.5       noise_mean = 0, noise_sd = 4     ), # model form for the first time point, given by model_form_x_t1     list(       effect = 0, model_form_x = model_form_x_t2, # from data: true_effect = 1.8       noise_mean = 0, noise_sd = 4     ), # model form for the second time point, given by model_form_x_t2     list(       effect = 0, model_form_x = model_form_x_t3, # from data: true_effect = 1.6       noise_mean = 0, noise_sd = 4     ), # model form for the third time point, given by model_form_x_t3     list(       effect = true_effect_long, model_form_x = model_form_x_t4, # from data: true_effect = 2.5       noise_mean = 0, noise_sd = 4     ) # model form for the fourth time point, given by model_form_x_t4   )    # =========== generate trial data ============   Data <- simulate_trial(X_int,     X_ext,     num_treated = 150,     OLE_flag = TRUE,     T_cross = 2,     outcome_model_specs   )     data_matrix_list[[trial_iter]] <- Data }

title: Introduction to rdborrow
text: rdborrow implements causal inference methods incorporating external controls randomized controlled trials (RCTs) longitudinal outcomes. package provides tools analysis simulation, enabling researchers evaluate different borrowing strategies design trials leverage external data. methods motivated SUNFISH trial spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), external controls olesoxime trial augment randomized data improve statistical efficiency.

title: Introduction to rdborrow
text: methods estimate average treatment effect (ATE) placebo-controlled phase borrowing external controls. methods support: borrowing (weight = 0): uses RCT data Optimal weight (weight = NULL): data-adaptive weight minimizing variance Fixed weight (weight = 0.3): user-specified borrowing amount Sandwich variance bootstrap inference See vignette("primary_analysis_workflow") usage.

title: Introduction to rdborrow
text: placebo-controlled phase, control subjects cross treatment. methods estimate long-term treatment effect using external controls remain untreated. OLE methods use bootstrap inference. See vignette("OLE_analysis_workflow") usage.

title: Introduction to rdborrow
text: simulation module evaluates estimator performance via Monte Carlo: simulate_trial() generates synthetic trial + external control data setup_simulation_primary() / setup_simulation_OLE() configure simulations run_simulation() runs Monte Carlo experiments reports bias, variance, MSE, coverage, power See vignette("primary_simulation_workflow") vignette("OLE_simulation_workflow") usage.

title: Simulate outcomes from additive linear models — simulate_outcome_from_model
text: X Data frame covariates. Numeric vector treatment indicators (length `nrow(X)`). outcome_model_specs List lists, one per time point. See Details . OLE_flag Logical. `TRUE`, time points `T_cross` use OLE model (patients treated). T_cross Positive integer. crossover time point separating primary OLE phases. used `OLE_flag = TRUE`.

text: element `outcome_model_specs` list : `effect` Numeric scalar. Treatment effect time     point. `model_form_x` Named numeric vector covariate     coefficients. Names must include `"1"` (intercept) match     column names `X`. `noise_mean` Numeric scalar. Mean normal noise. `noise_sd` Numeric scalar. SD normal noise.

title: Simulate outcomes from additive linear models — simulate_outcome_from_model
code: X <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(20), x2 = rnorm(20)) A <- rbinom(20, 1, 0.5) specs <- list(   list(     effect = 1.5,     model_form_x = c("1" = 2.0, "x1" = 0.5, "x2" = -0.3),     noise_mean = 0, noise_sd = 1   ),   list(     effect = 0,     model_form_x = c("1" = 1.0, "x1" = 0.2, "x2" = 0.1),     noise_mean = 0, noise_sd = 1   ) ) Y <- simulate_outcome_from_model(X, A, specs, OLE_flag = FALSE, T_cross = 2)
